readme: Registry of automations + critical outputs the health-heartbeat.ps1 watches for SILENT DEATH - an automation that stopped being scheduled (deleted/disabled), or an output that quietly went stale, WITHOUT a loud failure. Since 2026-08-22 health-heartbeat runs from the 'TC Grocery Capture Watchdog' task, moved to 10:30 on 2026-08-31 and RENAMED to 'TC Grocery Capture Watchdog 1030' on 2026-09-07 by ops/install-grocery-tasks.ps1 -FixName (the earlier ruling here said the 0930 name was deliberately not renamed; the registrar renamed it on the live scheduler at 06:30 and this registry did not hear, so the heartbeat paged one rename as two issues - a phantom TASK MISSING and an unwatched real task - at 10:30 the same morning. The registrar's $OWNED table and this registry MUST name the same tasks, and ops/install-grocery-tasks.ps1 -VerifyRegistry now checks exactly that on every push, through ops/audit-task-registry.ps1 in run-gates) (local-watchdog.ps1 and the SMP tasks are retired); capture-watchdog covers loud failures and the run record. Brad's rule 2026-08-22: Windows tasks are the ONLY routines that fire (no Claude scheduled agents) - every one belongs HERE, and health-heartbeat's REGISTRY DRIFT check pages if a 'TC *' or 'SMP *' task exists that is not listed. The rule was written when there were exactly three and said 'the three TC Grocery tasks'; two more were registered after it (TC Graph Nightly Matching 08-22, TC Recipe Harvest Crawl 08-24) and neither was added here, so each was unwatched from birth. Re-worded 2026-08-25 to state the rule that actually holds - a registry whose preamble contradicts its own contents teaches the reader to skip both. THE COUNT IS NOT THE RULE; THE REGISTRATION IS. Adding a task without adding it here is the defect, whatever the total. max_age_hours ~30 tolerates a late run + a weekend gap on a daily thing. Optional 'proves' (path or glob, repo-relative) names the output that shows the task's WORK actually landed: a nonzero exit whose proof output is fresh is reported as a warning, not paged as a death. The proof must be no older than the run it claims to prove. OUTPUT_FILES HAS A SECOND, OPT-IN FORM (2026-09-04, queue 2026-09-04-2feb5c): a writer that legitimately no-ops when its inputs have not changed gives its output no mtime liveness signal at all, so such a row declares 'currency_field' (the field inside the file that carries its currency stamp) plus 'currency_equals' (what that stamp must equal; only 'board_week', the newest grocery/out/comparison-<date>.json by name, is understood) and is judged on CONTENT instead. It is opt-in because the other four output_files rows are rewritten on every run and their mtime IS a real liveness signal - a default-on content check would silently disarm all four. Do not add these fields to a row whose writer cannot no-op, and do not widen max_age_hours to silence a no-op writer: see the CONTENT-CURRENCY block in health-heartbeat.ps1 for both rejected remedies.

windows_tasks.name: TC Grocery Ad Pulls 0700
windows_tasks.why: 07:00 weekly-ad pull for every store whose ad rolled over (capture-run -Kind ad; captures only, no chain). proves = the ads file itself: a run-log exists the moment the process starts, so proving with it downgraded a killed run (0xC000013A) to 'work landed'.

windows_tasks.name: TC Grocery Daily Capture 0800
windows_tasks.why: 08:00 quarterly-rotation capture + the ONE daily chain: compare -> guards -> publish -> recipes -> commit

windows_tasks.name: TC Grocery Capture Watchdog 1030
windows_tasks.why: 10:30 outcome check of the two tasks above (was 09:30 until 2026-08-31, and NAMED 0930 until 2026-09-07 when ops/install-grocery-tasks.ps1 -FixName renamed it on the live scheduler; it now runs AFTER the 09:45 alert-triage pass, so a board triage has already unblocked and republished is not reported as a failure - see Test-RunSuperseded in capture-watchdog.ps1) (schedule, run record, board, publish, ads, browser flags) + this heartbeat. EXITS 1 BY DESIGN whenever it has findings, and it is the script that RUNS health-heartbeat - without this flag the heartbeat pages about the watchdog every day the watchdog does its job (self-referential, permanent from its first real finding). KEEP allow_nonzero_exit ON THIS ROW: dropping it makes the heartbeat page TASK FAILED at 10:30 tomorrow when the watchdog exits 1 by design.

windows_tasks.name: TC Graph Nightly Matching
windows_tasks.why: 21:30 nightly graph matching (graph/pipeline/nightly.ps1 -HardStop 06:30 -MaxMinutes 150). Registered 2026-08-22, AFTER Brad's three-task rule was written, and never added here - so from that day nothing would have noticed if it stopped: health-heartbeat flagged it as TASK UNWATCHED every morning and the drift check is what finally named it (2026-08-24). proves = its own status stamp, which the run rewrites at the end; the task can exit 0 having done nothing, the stamp cannot.

windows_tasks.name: TC Recipe Harvest Crawl
windows_tasks.why: 18:00 daily recipe candidate crawl (meal-prep/pipeline/harvest-crawl.ps1). Registered 2026-08-24 and likewise never added here. proves = the dated crawl log, which is appended on every run including one that finds no new candidates; candidate-pool.json would have been the wrong proof because a legitimately empty crawl never touches it, and a proof that only exists on a good day pages on the ordinary ones.

output_files.why: public price feed every card fetches

this week's free-dinner rotation. REWRITTEN ONLY WHEN THE FREE SET FLIPS, so its mtime tracks the WEEKLY rotation, not the daily run that rotate-free-dinners.ps1 makes: the no-op early return at rotate-free-dinners.ps1:129-130 sits before the write at line 228. Judged on week_of, not on mtime. max_age_hours is kept here and is NOT consulted while currency_field is present - deleting the two currency_* fields is the rollback, and the number is left alone so nobody widens it (a window wider than the cadence never fires on time).
derived item->bid map (tools + top5 badges read it; regenerated daily)

external_files.label: recall-log.jsonl
external_files.why: the automatic-recall hook's offer log. Added 2026-09-08 (backlog I78): the recall hooks are the estate's newest automated loop and appeared in NO watch list, so the whole loop could stop firing and nothing would go red. A heartbeat is written by the watched thing and cannot separate 'found nothing' from 'never invoked'; this is the watcher watching on its own schedule, which is the only shape that can say this should have run and did not. 72h not 30h because the hook only writes when a session runs, and Brad does not work every day - a 30h window would page every quiet weekend and teach him to ignore it.

external_files.label: recall-reflex-log.jsonl
external_files.why: the reflex hook's fire log. Watched SEPARATELY from recall-log.jsonl rather than trusting one to prove the other: they are two different hooks on two different events, and the estate has already paid for assuming one signal covers two loops. Same 72h reasoning.

queues.name: recipe-specs-awaiting-propagate
queues.why: specs whose content changed since propagate last shipped them - the drain is propagate-recipes.ps1
queues.cost_if_undrained: corrected cards sit on disk and readers are served the old ones. On 2026-09-07 this was 120 cards and five days: the scaler fix, seventeen wrong-panel macro repairs, the Shop Smart bullet change.

queues.name: staged-ghost-writes
queues.why: writes an agent queued for approval instead of sending - the drain is ops/review-staged.ps1
queues.cost_if_undrained: an agent did the work and it never reaches the site. Armed for agent runs on 2026-09-07, so this queue starts existing now.

queues.name: open-triage-items
queues.why: ops alerts raised and not yet closed - the drain is triage, closing through grocery/triage-close.ps1
queues.cost_if_undrained: a live alert nobody answered. The queue de-dupes per type per day, so depth here is distinct conditions, not repeats.
